opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jacob Santos (employee ID E050) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E050.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Jacob Santos (E050) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. As a full-time employee, write is permitted (role owns Source Code, so admin is also allowed). Requested level write is within policy; recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security record for E050 shows contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors with basic training may have at most read access; write is not permitted. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommend read for Source Code.
reason: Conflicting records for E050: HR note lists employment as full-time (which would permit write for Source Code), while Security note lists contractor with basic security training (max access read). Since the contractor-based maximum (read) is the more restrictive binding constraint, and write would exceed it for a contractor, I grant the safe level permitted under both interpretations: read for Source Code.

- full_time: up to write (admin if role owns system). Engineer owns Source Code. So write is allowed.
- contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. This contractor has basic training, so max is read.

Note 2 says security record shows contractor with basic training. Note 1 says HR database shows full-time.

So Security looked up employment type in their own database and found contractor. HR looked up in their own database and found full_time.
